subject: Acme - Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up

Hey Jordan — great to meet you and Alex on today's discovery call. Quick recap + next steps on the pricing/rate limits items we discussed: 

1) Expected volume: you mentioned a primary use case generating ~10M tokens/day on peak days with steady-state ~2.5M tokens/day. Please confirm if that peak estimate is monthly burst or expected weekly spikes.

2) Target unit economics: you indicated a target of ~$800 - $1,200 per 1M tokens for predictable pricing. Our standard hosted price for the model profile we discussed is $900 / 1M tokens with quota-based rate limits; we can discuss a committed tier if you plan to reserve Dedicated capacity.

3) Rate limits & burst: default quota for a new account at this scale is 5 requests/sec per route with burst policy to allow short spikes up to 25 rps for up to 60 seconds. For bursts like your 10M token/day pattern, we recommend a quota increase + autoscale policy that allows short bursts and caps sustained throughput. Overage pricing for hosted is charged at 1.25x the unit rate for tokens above quota if a quota increase isn't approved in advance.

4) Overage and procurement: if procurement prefers no surprises we can add a soft cap with email alerts and require an explicit approval before allowing overage. Otherwise overages bill automatically but we can set a monthly spend ceiling for the first few months.

Attachments: attached our public rate card (redwood-rate-card-2026.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) that outlines capacity milestones and approval points.

Next steps: can you confirm the typical spike frequency (how many days/month you hit the 10M token peak), and whether your procurement team needs a fixed $/month commitment vs. pay-as-you-go? Once you confirm we'll propose either a committed Dedicated tier or an expanded hosted quota + trial period.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 10M token "peak" is something we see ~6-8 days/month (marketing campaigns + product launches), not every week. Steady-state ~2-3M/day otherwise.
- Our procurement team prefers a capped monthly cost during the first 3 months while we validate. Can you provide an example spend ceiling we could set that maps to the $/1M targets?
- For the burst policy: is the 25 rps/60s soft-burst automatic, or does it require approval? Also, if we hit sustained 30 rps for 10 minutes, what's the immediate behavior (throttle, queue, reject)?

Also looping in Alex from infra to make sure the technical constraints are covered.

—Jordan

Hi Jordan — thanks for the details, great context. Answers inline below and Rafael added a short note on runtime behavior.

- Peak frequency: 6-8 days/month is exactly the kind of burst profile our autoscale + burst buffers are built for. We can provision a monthly soft quota sized for your steady-state (2.5M/day x 30 ≈ 75M tokens/month) and allow controlled bursts to 10M/day on the specified days.

- Spend ceiling example: with our hosted rate of $900 / 1M tokens, a soft monthly ceiling equal to 150M tokens would map to $135k/month. If you prefer a guaranteed unit economics nearer $1,000 / 1M tokens, we can provide a 3-month committed tier at $950 / 1M with a 10% uplift on overages. If procurement wants no automatic overage billing, we can enable manual approval for any usage beyond the ceiling.

- Burst mechanics: the 25 rps/60s burst is automatic for short spikes. If you sustain 30 rps for 10 minutes, the system will start applying backpressure — requests will be queued briefly and then rejected with a 429 if the sustained rate exceeds the configured quota and autoscale cannot provision more capacity. We can configure a higher sustained quota or a temporary quota increase to avoid rejections during campaign windows.

Rafael, can you add a short note on how we handle token accounting across streaming calls and whether partial responses count toward the quota?

Next: if you can confirm whether procurement prefers the soft ceiling + manual approval or a short committed tier, we'll draft the procurement language and a DocuSign for approvals.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Alex Park <alex.park@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Rate limits & overage pricing follow-up

Hey Jordan — quick technical notes on token accounting and throttling behavior: 

- Token accounting: we count tokens produced and consumed per request. For streaming responses, tokens emitted in partial chunks are billed as they are produced; aborted or timed-out requests still incur token charges for the work done.

- Burst handling: short bursts are served from an adaptive buffer (no token loss). For sustained over-quota traffic the autoscaler attempts to add capacity; if capacity can't spin up fast enough, requests are queued (FIFO) up to a short window (~30s) then return a 429 with a Retry-After header. We can turn on a graceful-fallback policy that routes to a lower-cost model variant if you prefer to avoid hard 429s at the cost of quality.

- Overages: when a quota is exceeded and no manual approval is in place, overage tokens are billed at 1.25x the unit rate (we can negotiate that rate for committed volume). If you sign a 3-month commit we'll provide dedicated pool pricing and waive the first month's overage uplift.

I'll attach a short operations note to the mutual action plan and happy to walk Alex through the infra constraints if useful.

—Rafael
